verses.text: When Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, King Rezin of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to fight against Jerusalem, but they could not conquer it.
The royal family of David was told, "Syria has joined forces with Ephraim." So the hearts of Ahaz and his people shook, like trees in the forest shaking in the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out with your son Shear Jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the washerman's field.
Tell him: 'Be careful and stay calm. Do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of these two burnt out stumps of smoking firewood, the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria and of the son of Remaliah.
Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have made evil plans against you. They have said,
"Let us attack Judah and tear it apart. Let us divide it among ourselves and make the son of Tabeel king over it."
But this is what the Lord GOD says: "It will not stand. It will not happen."
For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is only Rezin. Within sixty five years Ephraim will be shattered and will no longer be a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is only the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, you will not stand at all.'"
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again and said,
"Ask the LORD your God for a sign. Ask for anything, from the deepest depths or from the highest heights."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not put the LORD to the test."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, family of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of people? Must you also try the patience of my God?
So the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.
He will eat butter and honey by the time he knows how to refuse evil and choose good.
For before the child knows how to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you are so afraid of will be left empty.
The LORD will bring on you, your people, and your father's family a time worse than any since Ephraim broke away from Judah. He will bring the king of Assyria."
On that day the LORD will whistle for the flies from the far streams of the Nile in Egypt, and for the bees from the land of Assyria.
They will come and settle in the steep valleys, in the cracks of the rocks, on all the thorn bushes, and in all the pastures.
On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates River, the king of Assyria, to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to cut off your beard too.
On that day a person will keep alive only one young cow and two sheep.
But they will give so much milk that the person will have butter to eat. Everyone left in the land will eat butter and honey.
On that day every place that once had a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be covered with briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows to hunt, because the whole land will be covered with briers and thorns.
You will no longer go to the hills that were once dug with a hoe, because you will be afraid of the briers and thorns. They will become places where cattle are let loose and where sheep walk around.
